condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable information is held or handled by an AI-mediated system or its dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: The source episodes identify distributed SDK release content within the participating AI-mediated workflow or dependent infrastructure.

condition_tests.literal_condition: An independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary restricts access, acquisition, disclosure or modification of that information for the actor, operation and context.
condition_tests.assessment: The independently evidenced boundary is the authorised publisher’s release integrity boundary and normal release lineage.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Occurrence evidence demonstrates that at least one such information operation crosses that boundary. A successful unauthorised retrieval or modification is sufficient; a theoretical route alone is not.
condition_tests.assessment: The realised operation is identified by the source-local decision: Compromised SDK versions were published through a trusted release identity outside the normal release lineage. Publication changed the protected package contents. This is distinct from whether a victim later executed credential harvesting.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Identifiable information and its independently evidenced confidentiality or integrity boundary are established for an AI-mediated system or dependent infrastructure.
condition_tests.assessment: This failure-occurrence decision does not assert successful-invariant for the same phase. The identified information and boundary are distributed SDK release content, governed by the authorised publisher’s release integrity boundary and normal release lineage.

condition_tests.literal_condition: A concrete access, acquisition, disclosure or modification attempt or operation materially tests that boundary.
condition_tests.assessment: This failure-occurrence decision does not assert successful-invariant for the same phase. The concrete test is: Compromised SDK versions were published through a trusted release identity outside the normal release lineage. Publication changed the protected package contents. This is distinct from whether a victim later executed credential harvesting.

condition_tests.literal_condition: Observed response or verification shows that the unauthorised information operation is prevented or that the operation remains within its authorised information boundary.
condition_tests.assessment: The evidenced boundary crossing is not verified confinement.

condition_tests.literal_condition: The protective conclusion is restricted to the tested information, actor, operation and route; the evidence supports that result rather than only a configured policy or a claimed repair.
condition_tests.assessment: The evidenced boundary crossing is not verified confinement.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The information is deliberately public for the assessed operation and no independent integrity or other access restriction governs that operation. Public readability does not authorise public modification.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The relevant restriction is the authorised publisher’s release integrity boundary and normal release lineage; this is not an unrestricted public read. Publicly readable packages/posts retain separately evidenced write restrictions where assessed.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The only material property is custody of authentication material. Assess Authentication Material Custody Integrity; separate private content or other protected information can independently engage this class.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The access finding concerns distributed SDK release content as protected information or a distinct record modification; any secret-only property is separately assigned to the custody class.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: The observed information operation is validly authorised within the independently established boundary. An approved test does not by itself authorise public release of protected information.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The assessed operation is tested against the authorised publisher’s release integrity boundary and normal release lineage. Technical access, research motivation or permission for another target does not authorise crossing this boundary.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Not aligned exclusion: Only a hypothetical vulnerability, exposed endpoint, unverified capability claim or unsuccessful attempt is established, without demonstrated protected-information access, acquisition, disclosure or modification.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The decision relies on the documented operation or named unresolved occurrence fact, not hypothetical severity: The Mistral advisory identifies unauthorised compromised SDK releases and a Python upload outside the normal release lineage. Package contents were changed through the trusted distribution surface. Public package readability does not authorise an unrelated party to replace its release content. No unobserved victim-secret exfiltration is inferred.

exclusion_tests.literal_exclusion: Class scope exclusion (all results): The issue is solely accuracy, availability, provenance, secondary-purpose permission or audit reconstruction, without an independently engaged information access or integrity boundary.
exclusion_tests.assessment: The independently engaged property is the authorised publisher’s release integrity boundary and normal release lineage; a solely accuracy, availability, provenance or audit result would not suffice.

independent_adjudication.no_additional_mapping_reason: The package publication supports information-integrity adjudication. A functional credential-harvesting payload without demonstrated victim-secret collection does not establish secret-custody loss.

Historical rows and seven-repair holds are preserved.
